headline: Highest risk is medium: Superset can ingest and act on upstream content, but this pair lacks a shared channel or direct evidence of harmful interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between awesome-production-machine-learning and Superset. A is a non-runnable curated list with no I/O surfaces; B exposes only the Superset API and allowlisted egress. Without a bridge, prompt injection via one into the other is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies content from A into B as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between them, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Review any copied content before pasting into Superset.
Disable any future shared MCP or message-queue bridge unless provenance is tracked.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows sensitive data classes touched, shared storage, or uncontrolled outbound transmission. A touches no data classes and has no egress; B has allowlisted egress but no secrets or PHI listed. With no documented shared workspace, leakage between them is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later pointed at sensitive datasets, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF a shared workspace is introduced, file-based leakage becomes possible.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in any shared directory.
Confirm Superset egress destinations remain allowlisted.
Reassess if either agent is connected to PHI, secrets, or financial records.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable and has no write surfaces, while B only exposes the Superset API and allowlisted egress. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only plausible conflict would require an added shared mutable resource not present in either profile, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same mutable resource, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator adds locking-free shared state, concurrent updates may collide.
mitigations: Avoid granting both agents write access to the same directory.
Use separate service accounts for any shared backend.
Add locking if a shared mutable resource is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can consume API-driven outputs and act as a BI layer, so if A's curated content is manually fed into B, B may render or operationalize it without verification. A itself is not runnable, which limits the pathway, but uncertainty about the integration should be treated as a real default-config risk once the pair is connected.
conditions: IF A's content is imported into Superset dashboards or metadata without review, B may propagate errors.
IF B is configured to trust imported content as authoritative, cascading error risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review before importing A-derived content into Superset.
Label imported content as untrusted in dashboards and metadata.
Add a verification step before any downstream action uses B's output.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. A is an open-source list with no data classes touched; B is open-source Superset with no secrets handled or data classes listed. The profiles do not establish a compliance breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is later routed through Superset, compliance must be reassessed.
IF deployment policies impose residency or retention constraints, verify them against the actual environment.
mitigations: Document the data classes each deployment will handle.
Check residency and retention settings before production use.
Reassess compliance if regulated data is introduced.
